Follow someone who empowers you in my stead.\\n\\nThe place, could mean either moving to another city, apartment, or just taking a walk. Move. Move your body. Take a hike in the woods without your phone, swim, hike, yoga, take a road trip, cross country or across town. Book a ticket to somewhere that you feel will change your life and immerse yourself when you arrive.\\n\\nAnd finally things, the toys and tools and food and phone. Too many are a burden. You‚Äôll usually find out what things you shouldn‚Äôt be hanging out with: if you eat bad food, your body will tell you. If you wear bad clothes, your friends will tell you, hopefully. My photography has been feeling stagnant, and I‚Äôve been pushing myself to shoot more film photography. This photo was taken on 35mm in that same effort to change the tools I use. You can usually bring the old thing back if you miss it too much.\\n\\nWhat if I can‚Äôt change them? Or worse yet, what if I don‚Äôt have the will or the drive to change them? Honestly, I don‚Äôt know the answer to that. I don‚Äôt have any answers at all, I‚Äôm finding. The struggles with these things and places and people are also the very things that make life worth pursuing. The bad apples you‚Äôve been hanging out with are apples too, we‚Äôre all just walking each other home. The places that drain you might have become better spaces because of you. The things that you shed are snakeskins, they‚Äôve served their purpose, however imperceivable that purpose may seem.\\n\\nSo I‚Äôll go, I‚Äôll start small, I‚Äôll change the camera I use today and something more significant some other day. ‚ÄúIf you don‚Äôt like where you are, move! You are not a tree!‚Äù an American author named Jim Rohn might have said that.

description: Earlier this year, @princetonupress sent me a copy of Francois-Xavier Fauvelle‚Äôs ‚ÄòThe Golden Rhinoceros: Histories of the African Middle Ages.‚Äô This book offers a stimulating introduction for those ‚Äì like me ‚Äì with only a murky understanding of this period in the continent‚Äôs history, and an opportunity to reflect on some of the historiographical problems current in medieval studies.\\n‚Ä¢\\nFauvelle‚Äôs book takes its name from the Golden Rhinoceros of Mapungubwe, a 13th-century gilded statuette unearthed in the 1930s. Unsupported by written documentation and excavated in less-than-ideal circumstances from an archaeological point of view, this precious object illustrates some of the key problems facing historians of medieval Africa. The histories Fauvelle wants to tell have been obscured by irreparable breaks in the oral traditions that preserved collective memory, and moreover by centuries of historical prejudice and academic neglect. But this is a book keenly aware of its own limitations. Rather than attempting to synthesise a coherent narrative over an entire continent through a thousand years, Fauvelle offers a ‚Äòjourney‚Äô through thirty-six vignettes. His focus is on the kingdoms and polities of sub-Saharan Africa rather than the Islamic empires of the Mediterranean coast, and some of the sites he describes are truly astonishing. We read of a mosque made of coral, entire villages built in salt, and whole churches carved from a single block of stone. The author seeks to dismantle the monolithic, unchanging ‚ÄòAfrica‚Äô of popular conception and to restore agency to the Africans whose histories he tells. The result is a fascinating introduction to a period of history that has for too long remained outside (or, at best, on the periphery of) the realm of medieval history as we tell it. The ‚ÄòMiddle Ages‚Äô are plural, and there is always room for more stories and for different perspectives.\\n‚Ä¢\\n‚Ä¢\\n‚Ä¢\\n#history #africa #africanhistory #medievalafrica #medieval #middleages #medievalworld #medievalhistory #medievalart #medievaltimes #medievalworld #medievalarchitecture #moyenage #medioevo #edadmedia #mittelalter #arthistory #historyofart #historylesson #gold #golden #rhino #african

description: Finlay, 18, skipped school to play with us. He messaged me on here when we landed and said he's not only the asst pro at Leven Links but also a member at Leven Thistle, one of the clubs that plays there. He gave us an incredible tour of his home course, pointed out lines and he's the rockstar who gave me the idea of marking out the number on the golf ball with three little lines. That's staying with me forever. The kid spends most of his swings on plane with a chipped SLDR driver and gets out typically 5 times a week. His latest hole in one was a few weeks back. What's interesting about all of this is that if we had just come here and played golf with ourselves - as tourists - we would have missed the entire point. That's just traveling to a patch of grass. We came to a country of people who love and who incredibly invented the wonderful game of golf. So when Jamie at @ayrshiregolfscotland said we had won the job, I requested extra tee times to include people like Fin - locals, employees, other travelers, caddies and whoever was around to join. We played Kingsbarns with 8 people walking and many other rounds similar. I do take the time to respond to all the messages here - I'm a bit behind now apologies, but I will get back to you - and what that means is that the world becomes a bit smaller... So for the vids - I can't exactly say for sure but I think the vlogs of this entire trip, the rounds, the time between shots, the off hours, the jokes, the lifetime moments like the big Old Course round w Stuart and his dad, my middle finger getting buzzed by the drone, Colt getting his first - and insanely in depth - taste of links golf, Hafer shooting the lens off his cam... All of that is coming a few weeks after we return so maybe early October, in what I'm thinking will be ten or so vlogs on my YouTube channel, subscribe at the link in my bio, I'm beyond excited to share. description: Imagine going to Paris and not eating a croissant? Imagine not eating bread, even though you aren‚Äôt gluten intolerant, because it‚Äôs a ‚Äòbad‚Äô carb. Yeah, that used to be me when I started this account. I used to follow a diet so strictly that I would deny myself certain foods because it wasn‚Äôt Paleo. Well, not sure if you‚Äôve noticed but Paleo Peach doesn‚Äôt post that many Paleo recipes anymore! I still eat nutritionally dense paleo-based foods (including my own recipes) a lot of the time. This type of food gives me energy and makes me feel amazing. However, I also eat not so paleo-based foods like pastries, chocolate, bread, cheese, sugar and drink alcohol because it tastes good and it makes me so freaking happy. And long term, I feel that‚Äôs way healthier than sticking to a rigid grain-free, sugar-free diet 100% of the time.\\n.\\nAs I navigate my way through life I am constantly evolving. That includes my food choices - right now I aim to eat nutritionally dense foods but also allow treats whenever I feel like it. And not raw, sugar-free treats, but real, sugary, rich treats. Treats that I wanted in the first place, so why make a substitute cake that has the same calories and same sugar content but it just came from a coconut instead of a sugar cane?\\n.\\nI‚Äôm also trying to make sustainable choices, by reducing my meat consumption, buying locally sourced and in-season foods and supporting small businesses. I‚Äôm only human and won‚Äôt always get this right, but I‚Äôm trying. And I would love for you to continue to support me in the direction that this page has been heading for a while. This isn‚Äôt a preachy post, or intended to drag any type of food choices a person may make, just an update on me and my life :) I will continue to post more about this later in the week.\\n.\\n#foodfreedom #intuitiveeating #antidietculture

He manages to combine a diverse range of subjects within his Instagram feed whilst still maintaining a consistent style. His compositions are elegant, minimal, and well thought out, and we particularly enjoyed his series shot in Peru. His photographs have a real sense of tranquility, and we are very proud to feature his work as today's Portfolio Post üòä\\n----------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\n@jeremy_plaisance: I‚Äôm Jeremy, a photographer based out of Sydney, Australia. I shoot professionally for a living which I‚Äôm grateful for, but I‚Äôd say I definitely got to a stage of feeling burnt out some years back from constantly shooting to a brief. It got to a point where the last thing I‚Äôd want to do is pull out a camera in my downtime. I think what pulled me out of that funk was discovering awesome street photography and minimalist urban and nature photography here on Instagram. There are just SO many talented photographers on this platform who inspired me through their work to pick up a mirrorless and start shooting for fun again.\\nThese days when I‚Äôm out and about with my little Fujifilm my aim is to just enjoy the simple interplay of texture, colour, shape, movement, pattern and light around me, and if I can find a composition where some of those elements harmonize to my eye, I‚Äôll take the shot. In that way, photography has become a kind of mindfulness practice for me, serving as a reminder of just how beautiful this planet can be, and that when life gets a little hectic or overwhelming, it can help to reduce things down to their simplest forms to find or even create examples of that beauty.\\n---------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\n@thecuriouscameraclub Portfolio Posts will be shared every Friday, Saturday and Sunday to celebrate the awesome community behind The Curious Camera Club (the World's Coolest Camera Club. Was it worth it?\\nI think it only made its next eight lives better. \\nThis urge to learn and understand others and our surroundings, and figure out ways to make our world better, is an innate instinct we all have. As well as helping society and technology evolve! But why would some people be much more curious than others?\\nHave you ever observed toddlers explore? They do it when their parents or care figures are relaxed, reassuring them that the environment is safe. Later on, they become more independent, assessing safety by themselves. We may have more knowledge and resources than toddlers, but the same is true for adults. If we are too insecure, if fear is too strong, it will block our curiosity! So unless we are just seeking thrills, we will tend to explore more when we feel safe. But we live in a society that doesn‚Äôt help us overcome fear, and even promotes a constant feeling of danger. Which stops our natural inclination towards curious behaviors, towards trying to understand what‚Äôs going on around us. Which keeps us put.\\nOnce again, I believe we can improve our lives and the world immensely if we look inward and figure out what fears are controlling us. And let go of the ones we don‚Äôt need anymore. description: First session back after 30 days of zero training. 100kg for lots of sets of 3 reps. It seems silly that I‚Äôm posting this video, but I‚Äôm posting it for a number of reasons.\\nThe first reason is to show how I ease my way back into training. My last session I squatted 280kg x 8 reps. I haven‚Äôt lost that much strength by taking the month off, I just know that whatever I do today I will pay for tomorrow. The first rule I have with training after a break is to walk out of the gym feeing like you could have done more. The reason I do this is because it allows me to progress as quickly as possible, back to proper weights without muscle soreness interrupting with my training. \\nThe next reason I‚Äôm posting this is to show that I still record my sets even though the weights are light. Just today a girl that I coach tried to describe her deadlift sets to me so I could critique her. I asked her if she recorded her sets and she said that the weight was too light, she felt embarrassed to record them in front of the people in the gym. This video recorder (iPhone) is my number one tool for giving me feedback on my technique. Recording my lifts isn‚Äôt just about posting videos on social media. It‚Äôs about making sure I‚Äôm doing everything right. I‚Äôm not embarrassed that I‚Äôm not lifting heavy. The girls in my gym we‚Äôre out lifting me today. That‚Äôs fine. I still need to make sure I was using the right technique, and I am my own harshest critic. \\nApart from all of that, it feels good to be back in the gym. My training frequency will be 6 sessions per week and I will do my main lifts 3 times per week, increasing the weight each time. I could have lifted more than this today, but I didn‚Äôt need to. There‚Äôs plenty of time for that.\\n#marathon #followthesystem @australianstrengthcoach @basegym

description: Christmas and plum cakes\\n\\nSo the snow has started and here comes the beautiful time of celebrations: the Christmas! the birthday of Lord Jesus. We give gifts; we eat cakes..in short, we enjoy the sweet moments with sweet people and eat delicious things like plum cakes. \\nPlumcake has a long tradition behind it. After a fasting what could be more joyful than to treat the tongue with sheer gentleness of plum cakes.. not only sweetness but they are full of healthy ingredients that help you stay healthy and warm. More often The cakes are made beforehand and are fed with brandy, sherry or whiskey which makes it even tastier and useful to keep warm.\\nSo let's celebrate this Christmas with the sense of sweetness within our hearts by being sweet and loving towards each other and let's eat plum cakes to remember and commemorate that sweetness. description: Corfe Castle is a 11th century medieval castle fortification standing above the village Corfe on the Isle of Purbeck in the English county of Dorset.  The castle was built by William the Conqueror, at Corfe soon after the Norman Conquest of England in 1066. The royal forest of Purbeck, where William the Conqueror enjoyed hunting, was established in the area. Between 1066 and 1087, William established 36 such castles in England. Sitting as it does on a hill top, Corfe Castle is one of the classic images of a medieval castle. \\nIn 1572, Corfe Castle left the Crown's control when Elizabeth¬†I sold it to Sir Christopher Hatton. Sir John Bankes bought the castle in 1635, and was the owner during the English Civil War. His wife, Lady Mary Bankes, led the defence of the castle when it was twice besieged by Parliamentarian forces. The first siege, in 1643, was unsuccessful, but by 1645 Corfe was one of the last remaining royalist strongholds in southern England and fell to a siege ending in an assault. Whatever I accomplish in my time as a teacher, I owe to these moments of study, & the long line of educators, like Dr. West, who made them possible. description: ‚öúÔ∏è Multan: The City Of Saints ‚öúÔ∏è .\\n\\n_____ . ‚öúÔ∏è Extremely overwhelmed by the amount of love I received in the first post I did for this series, I decided to dig deeper & find a place perhaps even most(if not all) Multanis wouldn‚Äôt know. After-all, the whole point of this series is to show you what others might not have. Throughout this series, I‚Äôll try my level best to create original content that you wouldn‚Äôt find elsewhere, esp on mainstream media & famous blogs(unless it‚Äôs after I post about that place of-course ;) ) ‚öúÔ∏è . .\\n\\n______ . . ‚öúÔ∏è So, with the thought of showing you guys something DIFFERENT & beautiful, I set out to a place even I hadn‚Äôt seen previously. And boy, did I get lost while trying to find it. In my almost dulhanon wala attire, it was a feat finding this well-hidden & surprisingly small gem of a place, but I‚Äôm extremely happy that I decided to visit it as it was beautiful beyond thought, if a little in need of funding & refurbishment. ‚öúÔ∏è . .\\n\\n_____ . . ‚öúÔ∏è Where Saints & Sufis are the essence of Multan, Love is the essence of this entire universe. Love motivates us, it‚Äôs the centre of our ambitions & our aspirations. We yearn, hope & long for love. We fight for love & we strive for love. Often times I find myself thinking about how love is a selfish feeling, how we mourn even the dead because of the pain & loss it causes us, not purely out of grieve for them. But after visiting this Tomb, one made in 1955 by a successful merchant & a loving husband Muhammad Suleman for his wife after her demise, I had a moment of stark clarity about love & why people chase after it their entire life: to belong & to be revered, even after they‚Äôre no more. ‚öúÔ∏è . .\\n\\n______ . . ‚öúÔ∏è Suleman kept building & renovating this tomb, with the help of a team of artists all the way from Agra up until his very last breath. description: This is the real reason I went to the Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum: to see this house by Kunio Maekawa (1905-86), one of Japan's greatest Modernist architects. Maekawa joined Le Corbusier's firm in Paris when he was 22, and became one of his key disciples in Japan. One of his lasting contributions to contemporary Japanese architecture was reviving the use of wood‚Äîa traditional material, and once which Maekawa began using in WWII, when other materials were in short supply. Built with a door at both ends so that it could still be used as a covered bridge and as a summerhouse. .\\n\\nA one up, one down dwelling, over the proceeding centuries it has been put to various uses including a weaving shop, a cobbler's, a chair maker's, an antique shop and at one time it even housed a family of eight - basket weaver John Rigg and his family of 6 children..I don't know how they fit!! In 1805 the building was used as a tea-room. I think a tea room is the best use for this little cutie!!\\n.\\nThese days Bridge house is in the care of the fabulous National Trust.\\n.\\nRight, we're off to Canterbury now. Reflect on the journey as this has led you to this very exact point in time.\\n\\nIt so easy to get lost in where we are heading we often forget where we have come from. description: Today I had the opportunity to spend time with some of the over 150 dogs rescued from a dog meat farm in South Korea by the Humane Society of the United States last month. These are just a few of the amazing animals that are now being rehabilitated at St Huberts Animal Welfare Center in New Jersey. Some were used as breeding machines and others were simply spending their lives in captivity waiting to be killed for food. They were kept outside in freezing cold weather, in wire bottom cages that cut and deformed their feet, and given small amounts of food and water together in one bowl, with no basic medical care  at all. After some time and love from the amazing people at St Huberts they are on the road to recovery, learning to trust people, and soon will be looking for the forever homes that they deserve. The Humane Society is deeply invested in closing down these farms and helping farmers convert their businesses to growing other food sources so that one day no dog will have to experience life in a meat farm. @humanesociety @sthubertsanimal üêæ

The fantastic big dome original crystal is in good conditions.\\n\\nThe really beautifully finished automatic caliber 2499 is running well with no issues. description: Shrouded in early morning mist, the Westbury White Horse looked particularly spectacular yesterday! Swipe ‚¨ÖÔ∏è for views and a 360 aerial video üòç 41.9km\\n.\\nBeing back in beautiful Wiltshire for a few days, I thought I would make a start on the white horse trail, which begins here at Westbury. I had been planning this hike for a few days and decided to start it at 5am, hopefully bagging a sunrise capture by the white horse too. Although too overcast to get the sun in the frame, the mist made it incredible and was a brilliant surprise!\\n.\\nIf you swipe to see the video, you can see how thick the fog was up on to Salisbury plain! My route took me anti-clockwise along the circular trail and yes, you guessed it, straight into that fog! For the first few hours, visibility was almost zero and it was quite eerie! üò∂ I made it to Pewsey, where there is another white horse, having spotted the Alton Barnes white horse on the way too. 3 white horses seen out of 8 so far, with a further 100km or so to go. I intend to complete the trail over another 3 sections over the next few months if I can üòä\\n.\\nThe Westbury White Horse was cut into the hillside some 400 years ago, to commemorate King Alfred‚Äôs victory over the Danes at the Battle of Ethandun in AD 878. As you can see, the views are extremely impressive and commanding - quite the site to have had the battle! I highly recommend checking it out - the car park is only a 100m stroll away from the white horse, so if you‚Äôre coming by car it is very easily accessible.\\n.\\nHave you seen any of Wiltshire‚Äôs white horses before?\\n.\\n#myweekendhike #timeforwiltshire #countryside #walkinguk #ramblersgb #ukpotd #lovegreatbritain #photosofbritain #visitbritain #capturingbritain #visitengland #explore_britain #igerswiltshire #photosofengland #mybritain #bestukpics #uk_greatshots #walking #hiking #hikingphotography #landscapephotography #droneshots #wiltshire #westbury #whitehorse #history #hikingadventures #dronephotography #dronephoto #dronestagram

description: Since recovering from my glute strain on the Colorado Trail back in September, I have spent the month of October focusing on diet and exercise. For all my off hiking seasons prior to this year, I have mostly just gone back into a routine of regular weight training at a gym, using a combination of machines, barbells, and dumbbells. And while that has produced various positive results for me, I don‚Äôt believe that it has ultimately been as beneficial towards the overall goals that I am trying to achieve. This year I wanted to try something new. Something that was more functional that contributed to a level of fitness that was total body. Key word in that being functional. And that‚Äôs why I have teamed up with @crossfitlbg in my hometown to help get me to where I want to be. You see, I still have lofty aspirations of competing in the field at the Barkley Marathons this coming spring. My FKT attempt on the Colorado Trail was part of the process for me, physically and mentally, to help me prepare for the Barkley. And while I wasn‚Äôt able to complete that, it still provided valuable lessons for me that I learned from and can apply as I progress toward my future goals. So over the course of the next 8 weeks, I will be continuing to utilize CrossFit to better build up my core strength and my overall level of fitness in congruence with all the various endurance training that I have been doing (hiking, running, trail running, swimming, rowing) to put me in the best physical position come January 1st. At that point, I will know whether I have been accepted as 1 of the 40 applicants that will have the opportunity to compete in the Barkley next year. Over the course of the next 8 weeks I will be increasing my endurance workload each week so that come January 1st, I will be able to jump off the deep end and strictly focus my time and energy on Barkley-specific training. I‚Äôve really been loving cross-training with CrossFit so far. Loving the hard work that is necessary to get better and stronger as well as loving the community and accountability that goes along with it. description: Sunday morning blog time, my friends. Please accompany me with a cup of something warm and read my thoughts. I‚Äôm blogging from the comforts of my bed (which should totally become a thing. I‚Äôm coining it ‚ÄúBed Blogging‚Äù üòâ). I had a strange moment last week. A minor upset happened and I was feeling the aftermath of it. I went for a walk in my neighbourhood as it was a beauty of a day. I was totally in my head stewing and a man crossed my path and with a warm and genuine smile he said, ‚ÄúI really hope you a spectacular day. I truly do.‚Äù And then he went about his way. \\nThis man was a complete stranger and the energy he emitted was radiant and lovely. \\nWell, that snapped me out of my funk immediately. After that quick encounter, I started to look around me. The leaves are starting to fall, the brightness of the sunshine, and the contrasts of light. \\nI then thought to myself that that man came right at the perfect moment. It‚Äôs almost like the Man Upstairs knew I needed a wee pick me up and sent an Earth angel to come just at the right time. \\nEven though it was something minor, I took it as something profound. We are Provided for. We are Taken Care of. \\nWe just need to pay attention. \\nIt‚Äôs all in the details. \\nI‚Äôm very thankful for the little moments and the big moments. That is what life is comprised of. \\nEnjoy your moments, loved ones. \\nWith extra gravy,\\nLindsay M. \\n#blog #blogger #life #beauty #autumn #blessed #awareness #vancouver #yvr #yaletown #thanksgiving #sundayblog

If you can hold it for 15 seconds then move to step 3. .\\n\\n3. Negative pull-up:  Get to the top most position of the bar.  Lower yourself down as slow as possible.  If you are able to take 10 seconds to lower yourself down then you may be ready to attempt a normal pull-up. description: It is Earth Day and this is probably the only ‚Äúday‚Äù I truly feel the urge to share about.\\n.\\nLook, I am not perfect. I drive a car and I put gas in it. Ini adalah berita baik untuk kami. Yang artinya kami perlu untuk mempromosikan lebih lanjut terkait ekosistem bisnis rintisan di Jakarta. description: Today is #worldmentalhealthday and I just wanted to say a few things. I hope that we can erase the stigma surrounding mental illness and raise awareness. I try to be open and honest when I write things like this. Sometimes it may be hard to get out of bed or do simple tasks. You may feel overwhelmed with sadness or worry. You may act distant. Mental illness is different for everyone. You never know what battles one may be facing regardless of how well you think you may know them. My advice is to find healthy ways to cope, to try your best to take the best care of yourself that you possibly can and to seek out professional help if you feel like you need it. Try to be there for the people in your life and check up on them every once in a while if you can. Find a good, stable support system and be there for others. description: Some days it is more difficult to summon confidence than others. You feel inadequate and pulled in every direction. It is hard to find the satisfaction when life gets busy like that. I am a perfectionist, and I don't like the feeling of not finishing a project to the best of my ability. My grandfather used to tell me that cycling teaches you humility. This got him clipping in to his pedals every day well into his 80's. He would say, each time he would get on his bike, he would know at any given moment there was someone better than him. But this didn't deter him from trying to get better at a craft he loved. All you can do is your best. This extends beyond sport. If I called him upset about being tired and failing, he would remind me that what I was doing was important and special. It wasn't about the bike, it was what I could do with the bike. I have found that I am able to find strength in all the other things I do and believe in, and that isn't necessarily on two wheels. I don't need confidence from results or watts. Those come and go. I find strength in my faith and family, investing in education and learning, and working on projects to provide inspiration and opportunity. Sitting here on the couch in my üè°, I realize that this bike is an excellent vessel to do just that. Find power. Share strength. Provide opportunity. Be generous with your kindness today. description: This week my friend Sarita @saritaarrazola visited me to teach me how to make tempeh! \\nI met Sarita in Guatemala three years ago and since then she started a local fermentation business, St. Pete Ferments @stpeteferments. It‚Äôs been amazing to watch her grow and introduce more people to healthy fermented foods!\\nShe brought her spores and her knowledge and I supplied the pigeon peas from my garden. I was quite excited! Before diving into the tempeh experiment we talked all about fermentation. She tasted my vinegars, sauerkrauts, honey wine and the current mango concoction I‚Äôm making with mango scraps. \\nI was happy with her feedback, nothing was bad, and all of it was pretty good to her, a professional!\\nAfter all that, we got started (well actually she got started and I made us banana ice-cream topped with honey and coconut flakes)!\\nThis was my first time making tempeh and her first time with pigeon peas. Two especially great things about tempeh right now are that it likes heat, so Florida summers are good for fermenting tempeh, and it takes less than 48 hours, unlike my krauts which like much cooler temperatures.\\nI‚Äôm excited to say the tempeh was a success. But‚Ä¶ I actually can‚Äôt eat it. I did grow the pigeon peas and I did make the tempeh, but I didn‚Äôt produce the spores. This year I am growing and foraging literally 100% of the food I eat. That means I‚Äôm only doing wild fermentation, which means capturing yeast and not buying any yeast or starters. Unless I can use a culture to grow my own culture...\\nIt‚Äôs time to do research on growing my own tempeh spores. Sarita gifted me a bag of tempeh spores, and I‚Äôm pretty confident I‚Äôll be able to grow my own with these, which will allow me to eat tempeh that is truly 100% homegrown.\\nFor now, I had my friend @marabouthomas taste it, and it passed his taste test.  Marabou came over to teach me how to make tortillas using my homemade flour. We made tortillas with yam flower, yuca flower, green banana flour and a mix of the three. This was my first bite of bread in 229 days. It was fantastic and I‚Äôm excited to make more.\\nTortillas and tempeh will both be big breakthroughs in adding diversity and deliciousness to my life!
